dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis maintained on Sep 3 with 5 of 8 indicators supportive: Global M2 at $103.4T rising on a 4-week basis, 2s10s steepening to +41bps, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.73T, BTC funding near zero at −0.0048%, and stablecoin dominance falling to 11.31% on a 30-day basis; three indicators neutral: ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6% (expanding but softening), DXY at 99.51 (neutral band), and real yields at 2.44% (flat 4-week trend lifts status from supportive to neutral as the 9bps August decline has fully reversed); BTC.D at 57.37% holds above the 55% alt-rotation threshold; pivotal macro cluster ahead: NFP Sep 4, ECB Sep 10, CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) held at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); June 2026 confirmed at $102.7T (MacroMicro); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (29th consecutive monthly increase, +5.4% YoY, record high, per FX.co); global M2 rose ~$0.7T over the prior 4-week window from ~$102.7T (June) to $103.4T (July composite); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global aggregate not yet published; 4-week uptrend confirmed (latest vs 4-week-prior composite); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); FOMC Sep 16 and ECB Sep 10 are the next key catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 10:00 AM ET: 54.6%, down 1.0 percentage point from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); below 55.2% consensus; Production 58.3% (vs July 58.5%), New Orders 53.7% (vs July 56.7%, −3.0pp), Employment 51.2% (vs July 52.8%); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising, not met; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62, neither applies); September ISM Manufacturing PMI (covering September activity) will be released on October 1—next reading; PMI at 54.6% corresponds to ~2.4% annualized real GDP growth; NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11 are the next macro inputs into the FOMC Sep 16 decision.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.51 on September 3, 2026 (down 0.05% from Sep 2 close of 99.69; source: web search aggregate); 4-week trend down: DXY was approximately 100.3–100.5 in early August 2026 and has declined to 99.51, a ~−0.9% relative change over 4 weeks, above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.51 within 97.5–100 neutral band); structural dollar weakness driven by Treasury buyback program, rate-cut expectations ahead of FOMC Sep 16, and ECB divergence; a dovish NFP (Sep 4) + CPI (Sep 11) cluster would accelerate DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory); a hawkish CPI surprise risks a move back above 100 (headwind territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (proxy-blocked; sourced via H.15/macrotrends): 2.44% as of Sep 1, 2026 (H.15 release); August 10 reading confirmed at 2.43%; August 31 confirmed at 2.44%; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% (Aug 4 estimate) → 2.44% (Sep 1) = +1bps, well within the flat threshold (≤5bps / ≤0.5% relative); the 9bps August decline (Jul 25 2.43% → Aug 27 2.34%) has fully reversed with a Sep 1 bounce to 2.44%; status neutral (4-week trend is flat, not 'rising', so headwind condition—rising AND above 2%—is not fully met; but trend is also not 'falling' and value is not below 1%, so supportive condition is not met either); status shifts from supportive (prior run) to neutral; CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16 remain the next compression catalysts for real yields.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 3, 2026: 10Y yield 4.79% (Sep 1, per web search), 2Y yield 4.38% (Sep 2, per Forbes/web search); implied spread +41bps (+0.41%); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 4 estimate) → +41bps (Sep 3) = +6bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed); FRED DGS10 and DGS2 proxy-blocked this run—values sourced from secondary web search aggregates; upcoming curve-shaping events: NFP Sep 4, ECB Sep 10, CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16; a dovish FOMC cut + soft data cluster would accelerate 2Y compression and further steepen the curve.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: ~$6.73T for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); Sep 3 H.4.1 release (week ending Sep 3) scheduled for 4:30 PM ET today—not yet indexed; FRED proxy-blocked this run; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (early August) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within flat threshold; routine measured QT continues at stable pace; no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat at post-2022 stabilization plateau; QT pace stable with no acceleration); next H.4.1 release will be the first Sep 3 week balance sheet data point.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately −0.0048% (CoinGlass proxy-blocked Sep 3 run; value held from prior verified observation, Aug 28, 2026; web search confirms funding near zero and slightly negative in late August / early September 2026); spot-driven price action with no levered long overextension signal; BTC.D at 57.37% on Sep 3 (above 55% alt-rotation threshold); Bitcoin price ~$77,600 (Sep 2-3, 2026 estimate); total crypto market cap ~$2.7T; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August and into September; well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; status supportive (near-zero and slightly negative funding, no long-side overextension); NFP Sep 4 is the next near-term catalyst for BTC funding behavior.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (Sep 3, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.7T (per web search, Sep 3, roughly flat in 24h); stablecoin dominance 11.31% ($305B / $2.7T); BTC.D 57.37% (Sep 3, above 55% alt-rotation threshold); Bitcoin price ~$77,600; 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% (early August 2026) to 11.31% (Sep 3), a sustained decline of ~2pp over 30 days; marginal day-over-day uptick (11.28% Sep 2 → 11.31% Sep 3) is noise within a clear 30-day downtrend; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rising—does not apply as total market cap is roughly flat); BTC.D above 55% keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast); ADP July +44K; a further contraction or weak rebound would strongly argue for a 50bps rate cut and push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; also includes unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, and labor force participation; initial jobless claims today (203K, week Aug 29) suggest no abrupt August deterioration in hiring.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—pipeline inflation read one day ahead of CPI August (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC Sep 16; PCE for July 2026 came in at 3.7% YoY (released Aug 26); a cooling PPI reinforces the disinflationary trend and supports rate-cut expectations; a hot print alongside hot CPI would strengthen the case for a hold and could pressure risk assets, pushing DXY above 100 (into headwind territory).

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6—penultimate labor read before FOMC September 16; released same day as PPI August and ECB rate decision; a spike above 220K would reinforce the rate-cut case one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before the FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 14:15 CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 14:45 CET—released the same day as US PPI and weekly jobless claims; a cut or hold with dovish forward guidance would be broadly supportive for global risk assets and euro-dollar crosses; released six days before the FOMC September 16 decision, making it a key cross-central-bank barometer for the global easing cycle; ECB policy divergence from the Fed is a near-term driver of DXY direction.
